1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# run-arms.sh — cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm driver (SDD D-2.3, DEC-0164, DEC-0171)
     4	#
     5	# Runs the declared control arms of one recall suite on a frozen fixture batch
     6	# against a detached git worktree pinned at --source-commit (never the live
     7	# tree), interleaving trials across arms so provider drift spreads evenly.
     8	#
     9	# Usage:
    10	#   run-arms.sh --suite review-recall|audit-recall --arms a,b,c
    11	#               --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,… --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
    12	#               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
    13	#               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
    14	#               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
    15	#
    16	# Per trial (fixture × arm × trial), in this order:
    17	#   1. the fixture's SHA256SUMS entries (its files, hidden manifest and labels)
    18	#      are verified; a drift stops the batch (state failed, exit 3). The whole
    19	#      corpus is verified once at batch start (digest in MANIFEST.json); each
    20	#      row records the SHA256SUMS digest seen at its trial, so approving another
    21	#      fixture's labels mid-batch is visible and harmless
    22	#   2. evals/harness/sandbox.sh creates the sandbox from the frozen fixture
    23	#   3. execute-agent.sh runs the executor with EVAL_PROMPT_TREE = the pinned
    24	#      worktree, LOA_EVAL_ARM = the arm (toggles hit the sandbox copy only),
    25	#      LOA_EVAL_SOURCE_COMMIT, EVAL_MODEL
    26	#   4. grade.sh grades it; the row goes to <batch>/<arm>/results.jsonl with
    27	#      arm, trial, source_commit, model_id, seed (null: the CLI route takes
    28	#      none) and run_date; the artifacts go under <batch>/<arm>/artifacts/
    29	#   A trial whose executor fails for a transport reason (timeout, no result
    30	#   event, API error, rate or session limit) is retried once after
    31	#   --retry-wait seconds; a second failure records an error row and the arm
    32	#   ends `partial`. Other executor failures are recorded, not retried.
    33	#
    34	# Layout: <results-dir>/<suite>/<batch>/{MANIFEST.json,STATUS.json,run.log,
    35	#   <arm>/results.jsonl,<arm>/artifacts/…}; <results-dir>/<suite>/STATUS.json
    36	#   aggregates every batch of the suite (the Sprint 2 gate and report.sh
    37	#   --arms read it). STATUS.json: {state: running|complete|partial|failed,
    38	#   per_arm: {<arm>: {trials_done, trials_failed, trials_planned}},
    39	#   source_commit, model_id, started, finished}.
    40	#
    41	# Exit: 0 complete, 1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept),
    42	#       2 usage / refused before starting, 3 failed (no trial completed, or
    43	#       the corpus drifted mid-run)
    44	#
    45	# Executor: Fable 5.1 (D33, DEC-0164); the default --model is the id the
    46	# local claude CLI accepted on the cycle-129 probe (claude-fable-5-1).
    47	# Tested by evals/tests/run-arms.bats (stubbed CLI; no model call).
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    53	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    54	EVALS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/evals"
    55	CORPUS_DIR="$EVALS_DIR/fixtures/review-prs"
    56	DEFAULT_MODEL="claude-fable-5-1"
    57	CACHE_ROOT="${LOA_ARMS_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/loa/cycle-129}"
    58	# the repository the pinned source worktree is cut from (tests point it at a
    59	# throwaway repo so they never register a worktree in the real one)
    60	SOURCE_REPO="${LOA_ARMS_SOURCE_REPO:-$REPO_ROOT}"
    61	
    62	SUITE="" ARMS_CSV="" FIXTURES_CSV="" TRIALS="" SOURCE_COMMIT="" MODEL="$DEFAULT_MODEL"
    63	CONCURRENCY=2 BATCH="" RESULTS_ROOT="$EVALS_DIR/results/arms" RETRY_WAIT=300
    64	DRY_RUN=false ALLOW_UNAPPROVED=false
    65	
    66	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,46p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    67	die() { echo "run-arms: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    68	
    69	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    70	  case "$1" in
    71	    --suite) SUITE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    72	    --arms) ARMS_CSV="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    73	    --fixtures) FIXTURES_CSV="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    74	    --trials) TRIALS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    75	    --source-commit) SOURCE_COMMIT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    76	    --model) MODEL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    77	    --concurrency) CONCURRENCY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    78	    --batch) BATCH="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    79	    --results-dir) RESULTS_ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    80	    --retry-wait) RETRY_WAIT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    81	    --allow-unapproved) ALLOW_UNAPPROVED=true; shift ;;
    82	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=true; shift ;;
    83	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    84	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    85	  esac
    86	done
    87	
    88	# --- validate arguments ------------------------------------------------------
    89	case "$SUITE" in review-recall|audit-recall) ;; *) die "--suite must be review-recall or audit-recall" ;; esac
    90	[[ "$TRIALS" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]?$ ]] || die "--trials must be an integer 1-99"
    91	[[ "$CONCURRENCY" =~ ^[1-9]$ ]] || die "--concurrency must be 1-9"
    92	[[ "$RETRY_WAIT" =~ ^[0-9]{1,5}$ ]] || die "--retry-wait must be whole seconds"

   132	# verify_corpus [<fixture>] — every SHA256SUMS entry (or one fixture's entries
   133	# and its manifest) hashes as recorded. Prints the SHA256SUMS digest.
   134	verify_corpus() {
   135	  python3 -I - "$CORPUS_DIR" "${1:-}" <<'PY'
   136	import hashlib, os, sys
   137	corpus, only = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   138	sums = os.path.join(corpus, "SHA256SUMS")
   139	raw = open(sums, "rb").read()
   140	bad = []
   141	for line in raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines():
   142	    if not line.strip():
   143	        continue
   144	    digest, rel = line.split("  ", 1)
   145	    if only and not (rel.startswith(only + "/") or rel == f"manifests/{only}.json" or rel == "corpus.tsv"
   146	                     or rel.startswith(f"labels/{only}.")):
   147	        continue
   148	    p = os.path.join(corpus, rel)
   149	    if not os.path.isfile(p) or hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != digest:
   150	        bad.append(rel)
   151	if bad:
   152	    print("corpus drift: " + ", ".join(bad[:10]), file=sys.stderr)
   153	    sys.exit(1)
   154	print(hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
   155	PY
   156	}

     2	"""arms-report.py — the cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm report (SDD D-2.3).
     3	
     4	Invoked by `report.sh --arms`. Reads <results-root>/<suite>/STATUS.json (the
     5	suite aggregate run-arms.sh writes), every batch's MANIFEST.json and
     6	<arm>/results.jsonl, and the suite's pre-registered `ab.threshold` and
     7	`ab.arms`, and writes one markdown report.
     8	
     9	Per arm: recall (mean over defect fixtures of the per-fixture trial mean;
    10	the min, max and spread of the per-trial means), refuted share (cited
    11	findings matching neither a feedback label nor a fix region, over cited
    12	findings, pooled over completed trials), tokens per call, the percentile
    13	bootstrap interval of the recall drop (baseline - arm) resampling fixtures,
    14	the verdict and the missed labels.
    15	
    16	Verdict (pre-registered; never computed for baseline):
    17	  inconclusive  --partial; the run is not complete; a planned fixture lacks
    18	                trials_required completed trials in the arm or the baseline;
    19	                model or source skew; no defect fixture; or only a recall
    20	                rule is violated while the mean drop does not exceed the
    21	                baseline's own trial-to-trial spread (a change too small to name)
    22	  recall loss   the refuted-share rule is violated, or a recall rule is
    23	                violated and the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread
    24	  no recall loss  every rule holds:
    25	                  upper bound of the drop interval <= mean_recall_max_drop
    26	                  arm min trial mean >= baseline min trial mean - min_trial_recall_max_drop
    27	                  arm refuted share <= baseline refuted share + refuted_share_max_rise
    28	An `informational: true` arm's verdict reports a yield only.
    29	
    30	Exit: 0 written, 1 refused (a suite is not complete and --partial was not
    31	given), 2 error. Stdlib only.
    32	"""
    33	import argparse
    34	import datetime
    35	import json
    36	import os
    37	import random
    38	import sys
    39	from collections import Counter, defaultdict

    42	def load_yaml_subset(path):
    43	    """The suites are YAML (no stdlib parser); the harness already depends on yq v4."""
    44	    import subprocess
    45	    out = subprocess.run(["yq", "-o=json", ".", path], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    46	    return json.loads(out)

    49	def read_jsonl(path):
    50	    rows = []
    51	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
    52	        return rows
    53	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    54	        for line in fh:
    55	            line = line.strip()
    56	            if line:
    57	                try:
    58	                    rows.append(json.loads(line))
    59	                except ValueError:
    60	                    continue
    61	    return rows

    64	def mean(xs):
    65	    xs = [x for x in xs if x is not None]
    66	    return sum(xs) / len(xs) if xs else None
    67	
    68	
    69	def fmt(x, nd=3):
    70	    return "n/a" if x is None else f"{x:.{nd}f}"

    73	def recall_details(row):
    74	    for g in row.get("graders") or []:
    75	        if g.get("name") == "recall-vs-defects.sh" and isinstance(g.get("details"), dict):
    76	            return g["details"]
    77	    return None
    78	
    79	
    80	def tokens(row):
    81	    u = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("usage") or {}
    82	    if not u:
    83	        return None
    84	    return sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
    85	               ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
    86	
    87	
    88	def percentile(sorted_xs, q):
    89	    if not sorted_xs:
    90	        return None
    91	    k = max(0, min(len(sorted_xs) - 1, int(round(q * (len(sorted_xs) - 1)))))
    92	    return sorted_xs[k]
    93	
    94	
    95	def bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, seed):
    96	    """Percentile bootstrap of the mean of per-fixture deltas (resample fixtures)."""
    97	    if not deltas:
    98	        return None, None
    99	    rng = random.Random(seed)
   100	    n = len(deltas)
   101	    means = sorted(sum(deltas[rng.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(iterations))
   102	    a = (1.0 - level) / 2.0
   103	    return percentile(means, a), percentile(means, 1.0 - a)
   104	
   105	
   106	class Arm:
   107	    def __init__(self, arm_id):
   108	        self.id = arm_id
   109	        self.cells = defaultdict(list)   # fixture -> [(trial, recall)], every completed trial kept
   110	        self.planted = {}                # fixture -> planted count
   111	        self.cited = 0
   112	        self.refuted = 0
   113	        self.tokens = []
   114	        self.models = set()
   115	        self.sources = set()
   116	        self.done = 0
   117	        self.errors = 0
   118	        self.fallback_trials = 0         # trials the CLI moved to another model on a safeguard refusal
   119	        self.fallback_kinds = Counter()
   120	        self.missed = Counter()          # (fixture, label) -> trials missed
   121	        self.seen = Counter()            # (fixture, label) -> trials graded
   122	
   123	    def add(self, row):
   124	        if row.get("status") != "completed":
   125	            self.errors += 1
   126	            return
   127	        d = recall_details(row)
   128	        if d is None:
   129	            self.errors += 1
   130	            return
   131	        self.done += 1
   132	        fx = row.get("fixture") or row.get("task_id", "").split("-", 1)[-1]
   133	        self.planted[fx] = int(d.get("planted") or 0)
   134	        if d.get("recall") is not None:
   135	            self.cells[fx].append((int(row.get("trial") or 0), float(d["recall"])))
   136	        if d.get("findings_cited") is not None:
   137	            self.cited += int(d.get("findings_cited") or 0)
   138	            self.refuted += int(d.get("findings_refuted") or 0)
   139	        t = tokens(row)
   140	        if t is not None:
   141	            self.tokens.append(t)
   142	        self.models.add(row.get("model_id") or (row.get("executor") or {}).get("model_id"))
   143	        # every model that produced output in the call (an auxiliary model is skew too)
   144	        for mid, out in ((row.get("executor") or {}).get("models_used") or {}).items():
   145	            if out:
   146	                self.models.add(mid)
   147	        fb = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("refusal_fallbacks") or []
   148	        if fb:
   149	            self.fallback_trials += 1
   150	            for x in fb:
   151	                self.fallback_kinds[f"{x.get('from')}→{x.get('to')} ({x.get('category')})"] += 1
   152	        self.sources.add(row.get("source_commit") or (row.get("executor") or {}).get("source_commit"))
   153	        for lbl in d.get("missed") or []:
   154	            self.missed[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   155	            self.seen[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   156	        for lbl in d.get("detected") or []:
   157	            self.seen[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   158	
   159	    def defect_fixtures(self):
   160	        return sorted(f for f, p in self.planted.items() if p > 0 and self.cells.get(f))
   161	
   162	    def fixture_means(self):
   163	        return {f: mean([r for _t, r in self.cells[f]]) for f in self.defect_fixtures()}
   164	
   165	    def trial_means(self):
   166	        by_trial = defaultdict(list)
   167	        for f in self.defect_fixtures():
   168	            for t, r in self.cells[f]:
   169	                by_trial[t].append(r)
   170	        return {t: mean(v) for t, v in sorted(by_trial.items())}
   171	
   172	    def refuted_share(self):
   173	        return self.refuted / self.cited if self.cited else None

   176	def suite_report(root, suites_dir, suite, partial, out_lines):
   177	    sdir = os.path.join(root, suite)
   178	    status = {}
   179	    sp = os.path.join(sdir, "STATUS.json")
   180	    if os.path.isfile(sp):
   181	        status = json.load(open(sp, encoding="utf-8"))
   182	    spec = load_yaml_subset(os.path.join(suites_dir, f"{suite}.yaml"))
   183	    ab = spec.get("ab") or {}
   184	    th = ab.get("threshold") or {}
   185	    arm_meta = {a["id"]: a for a in ab.get("arms") or []}
   186	    trials_required = int(th.get("trials_required", 3))
   187	    max_drop = float(th.get("mean_recall_max_drop", 0.10))
   188	    min_trial_drop = float(th.get("min_trial_recall_max_drop", 0.15))
   189	    refuted_rise = float(th.get("refuted_share_max_rise", 0.10))
   190	    bs = th.get("bootstrap") or {}
   191	    iterations = int(bs.get("iterations", 2000))
   192	    level = float(bs.get("level", 0.90))
   193	
   194	    planned_fx, planned_arms, manifests = set(), [], []
   195	    arms = {}
   196	    for batch in sorted(os.listdir(sdir)) if os.path.isdir(sdir) else []:
   197	        bdir = os.path.join(sdir, batch)
   198	        mp = os.path.join(bdir, "MANIFEST.json")
   199	        if not os.path.isfile(mp):
   200	            continue
   201	        m = json.load(open(mp, encoding="utf-8"))
   202	        if m.get("dry_run"):
   203	            continue
   204	        manifests.append(m)
   205	        planned_fx.update(m.get("fixtures") or [])
   206	        for a in m.get("arms") or []:
   207	            if a not in planned_arms:
   208	                planned_arms.append(a)
   209	            arm = arms.setdefault(a, Arm(a))
   210	            for row in read_jsonl(os.path.join(bdir, a, "results.jsonl")):
   211	                arm.add(row)
   212	    order = [a for a in arm_meta if a in arms] + [a for a in planned_arms if a not in arm_meta]
   213	    state = status.get("state", "unknown")
   214	    complete = state == "complete"
   215	
   216	    out_lines.append(f"## {suite}")
   217	    out_lines.append("")
   218	    out_lines.append(f"- STATUS: `{state}`; batches: {', '.join(b.get('batch', '?') for b in status.get('batches', [])) or 'none'}")
   219	    srcs = sorted({m.get('source_commit') for m in manifests})
   220	    models = sorted({m.get('model_id') for m in manifests})
   221	    out_lines.append(f"- source commit(s): {', '.join(f'`{s[:12]}`' for s in srcs if s) or 'n/a'}; executor model requested: {', '.join(f'`{x}`' for x in models if x) or 'n/a'}")
   222	    out_lines.append(f"- planned fixtures ({len(planned_fx)}): {', '.join(sorted(planned_fx)) or 'none'}")
   223	    out_lines.append(f"- threshold: trials_required {trials_required}, mean_recall_max_drop {max_drop}, "
   224	                     f"min_trial_recall_max_drop {min_trial_drop}, refuted_share_max_rise {refuted_rise}, "
   225	                     f"bootstrap {bs.get('method', 'percentile')} {level} over {bs.get('resample', 'fixtures')} x{iterations}")
   226	    out_lines.append("")
   227	
   228	    base = arms.get("baseline")
   229	    base_fm = base.fixture_means() if base else {}
   230	    base_tm = base.trial_means() if base else {}
   231	    base_spread = (max(base_tm.values()) - min(base_tm.values())) if base_tm else None
   232	    base_min = min(base_tm.values()) if base_tm else None
   233	    base_ref = base.refuted_share() if base else None
   234	
   235	    def coverage_gaps(arm):
   236	        gaps = []
   237	        for fx in sorted(planned_fx):
   238	            planted = arm.planted.get(fx)
   239	            n = len(arm.cells.get(fx, [])) if planted else 0
   240	            if planted == 0:
   241	                continue  # a clean fixture carries no recall; refuted share only
   242	            if n < trials_required:
   243	                gaps.append(f"{fx} {n}/{trials_required}")
   244	        return gaps
   245	
   246	    header = ("| arm | trials done | errors | mean recall | min | max | spread | drop vs baseline | "
   247	              f"{int(level * 100)}% CI of drop | refuted share | tokens/call | verdict |")
   248	    out_lines.append(header)
   249	    out_lines.append("|" + "---|" * 12)
   250	    details = []
   251	    verdicts = {}
   252	    for a in order:
   253	        arm = arms[a]
   254	        fm = arm.fixture_means()
   255	        tm = arm.trial_means()
   256	        m = mean(list(fm.values()))
   257	        mn = min(tm.values()) if tm else None
   258	        mx = max(tm.values()) if tm else None
   259	        spread = (mx - mn) if tm else None
   260	        rs = arm.refuted_share()
   261	        tok = mean(arm.tokens)
   262	        drop = lo = hi = None
   263	        reasons = []
   264	        if a == "baseline":
   265	            verdict = "(reference)"
   266	        else:
   267	            common = sorted(set(fm) & set(base_fm))
   268	            deltas = [base_fm[f] - fm[f] for f in common]
   269	            drop = mean(deltas)
   270	            lo, hi = bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, f"{suite}:{a}")
   271	            if partial:
   272	                reasons.append("--partial report")
   273	            if not complete:
   274	                reasons.append(f"run state is {state}")
   275	            if base is None:
   276	                reasons.append("no baseline arm")
   277	            gaps = coverage_gaps(arm) + ([f"baseline {g}" for g in coverage_gaps(base)] if base else [])
   278	            if gaps:
   279	                reasons.append("coverage: " + ", ".join(gaps[:8]) + (" …" if len(gaps) > 8 else ""))
   280	            mods = {x for x in arm.models | (base.models if base else set()) if x}
   281	            if len(mods) > 1:
   282	                reasons.append("model skew: " + ", ".join(sorted(mods)))
   283	            srcs_a = {x for x in arm.sources | (base.sources if base else set()) if x}
   284	            if len(srcs_a) > 1:
   285	                reasons.append("source skew: " + ", ".join(sorted(s[:12] for s in srcs_a)))
   286	            if not deltas:
   287	                reasons.append("no defect fixture graded in both arms")
   288	            if reasons:
   289	                verdict = "inconclusive"
   290	            else:
   291	                violated, refuted_violated = [], False
   292	                if hi is None or hi > max_drop:
   293	                    violated.append(f"drop CI upper {fmt(hi)} > {max_drop}")
   294	                if mn is None or base_min is None or mn < base_min - min_trial_drop:
   295	                    violated.append(f"min trial {fmt(mn)} < baseline min {fmt(base_min)} - {min_trial_drop}")

   297	                    violated.append(f"refuted share {fmt(rs)} > baseline {fmt(base_ref)} + {refuted_rise}")
   298	                    refuted_violated = True
   299	                if not violated:
   300	                    verdict = "no recall loss"
   301	                elif (not refuted_violated and drop is not None and base_spread is not None

   304	                    # baseline moves against itself: too small a change to name
   305	                    verdict = "inconclusive"
   306	                    reasons.append("rule violated (" + "; ".join(violated) + f") but |drop| {fmt(abs(drop))} "
   307	                                   f"<= baseline spread {fmt(base_spread)}: no change can be named")
   308	                else:
   309	                    verdict = "recall loss"
   310	                    reasons.extend(violated)
   311	            if (arm_meta.get(a) or {}).get("informational"):
   312	                verdict += " (informational: yield only)"
   313	        verdicts[a] = verdict
   314	        out_lines.append(
   315	            f"| `{a}` | {arm.done} | {arm.errors} | {fmt(m)} | {fmt(mn)} | {fmt(mx)} | {fmt(spread)} | "
   316	            f"{fmt(drop)} | {('[' + fmt(lo) + ', ' + fmt(hi) + ']') if lo is not None else 'n/a'} | "
   317	            f"{fmt(rs)} | {('%.0f' % tok) if tok is not None else 'n/a'} | **{verdict}** |")
   318	        if arm.fallback_trials:
   319	            reasons.append(f"{arm.fallback_trials}/{arm.done} trial(s) fell back to another model on a safeguard refusal: "
   320	                           + ", ".join(f"{k} x{n}" for k, n in arm.fallback_kinds.most_common()))
   321	        if reasons:
   322	            details.append(f"- `{a}`: " + "; ".join(reasons))
   323	        if a != "baseline" and drop is not None and base_spread is not None:
   324	            named = "named" if abs(drop) > base_spread else "not named (within the baseline's own spread)"
   325	            details.append(f"- `{a}`: mean drop {fmt(drop)} vs baseline spread {fmt(base_spread)}: change {named}")
   326	    out_lines.append("")
   327	    if details:
   328	        out_lines.append("Verdict notes:")
   329	        out_lines.extend(details)
   330	        out_lines.append("")
   331	    out_lines.append("### Missed labels")
   332	    out_lines.append("")
   333	    for a in order:
   334	        arm = arms[a]
   335	        items = sorted(arm.missed.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))
   336	        if not items:
   337	            out_lines.append(f"- `{a}`: none")
   338	            continue
   339	        shown = ", ".join(f"{fx}:{lbl} ({n}/{arm.seen[(fx, lbl)]})" for (fx, lbl), n in items[:40])
   340	        more = f" … and {len(items) - 40} more" if len(items) > 40 else ""
   341	        out_lines.append(f"- `{a}`: {shown}{more}")

   344

   346	def main():
   347	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   348	    ap.add_argument("--results-root", required=True)
   349	    ap.add_argument("--suites-dir", required=True)

   352	    ap.add_argument("--partial", action="store_true")

   356	    suites = [s for s in args.suites.split(",") if s] or sorted(

   360	        return 2
   361	    for s in suites:
   362	        if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(args.results_root, s)):
   363	            print(f"arms-report: no results for suite {s} under {args.results_root}", file=sys.stderr)
   364	            return 2
   365	        st = {}
   366	        sp = os.path.join(args.results_root, s, "STATUS.json")

   375	    lines = [f"# Control-arm report — {args.date}", ""]

   378	                  "below reads `inconclusive` and none licenses a deletion (SDD D-2.3).", ""]
   379	    lines += ["Generated by `evals/harness/report.sh --arms` from `" + args.results_root + "`. "
   380	              "Recall is graded by `recall-vs-defects.sh` (planted defects and approved record labels); "
   381	              "refuted share counts cited findings that match neither a label nor a fix region. "

   383	    for s in suites:

   387	        fh.write("\n".join(lines).rstrip() + "\n")

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# =============================================================================
3	# seed-corpus-from-record.sh — build a review-recall fixture from a shipped
4	# sprint's round-1 state and its record-branch feedback (cycle-129 FR-2,
5	# SDD D-2.2, DEC-0154)
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh <global-sprint> <record-ref> [--out <corpus>/pr-NN]
9	#                              [--base <rev>] [--head <rev>] [--fix <rev>]
10	#                              [--feedback a.md,b.md] [--dry-run]
11	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --build-manifest pr-NN   # labels → hidden manifest (after curation)
12	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <YYYY-MM-DD>"
13	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --freeze                 # regenerate SHA256SUMS
14	#   seed-corpus-from-record.sh --check                  # verify SHA256SUMS
15	#   common: [--repo <git dir>] [--corpus <evals/fixtures/review-prs>]
16	#
17	# Without --base/--head/--fix/--feedback/--out the sprint's row in
18	# <corpus>/record-pairs.tsv supplies them.
19	#
20	# Writes (seed):
21	#   <corpus>/pr-NN/{fixture.yaml, head.diff, PR.md, REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md,
22	#                   AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md, base/…, head/…}     (copied into the sandbox)
23	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.tsv          HIDDEN (never copied into a sandbox): the labels,
24	#                                      first line `# approved-by: pending`
25	#   <corpus>/labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt  HIDDEN: every finding that did not become a label, and why
26	#   <corpus>/manifests/pr-NN.json      HIDDEN: the graded manifest (`approved: false` until --approve)
27	#   <corpus>/corpus.tsv                one `record` row per fixture (or a `#` gap comment)
28	#   evals/tasks/{review,audit}-recall/{review,audit}-pr-NN.yaml
29	#   <corpus>/SHA256SUMS                refreshed
30	#
31	# Scope: the fixture is the change base..head without the generated or state

# =============================================================================
# sprint: '### Seams Under Test' per sprint block (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.2)
# =============================================================================
# Gated on the plan header's **Date:** (the first one before the first H2): from
# SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM on, every '## Sprint N' block (up to the next H2) must carry
# the block with at least one table row below its separator line; older and
# undated plans WARN once, except that a live plan (under grimoires/loa/, not its
# archive/) without a parseable header date fails. Fenced code is tracked by
# lib/md-fence.awk (CommonMark lengths and characters); headings inside it do not count.
SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM="2026-10-13"

# @guard validator:sprint.seams
validate_sprint_seams() {
    local fence_src
    if ! fence_src="$(cat "${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/md-fence.awk" 2>/dev/null)" || [[ -z "$fence_src" ]]; then
        violations+=("cannot read ${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/md-fence.awk; the sprint Seams check needs it (reinstall the framework scripts)")
        return 0
    fi
    local plan_date
    plan_date="$(LC_ALL=C awk "$fence_src"'
        md_fence($0) { next }
        /^## / { exit }
        /^\*\*Date:?\*\*:?/ { if (match($0, /[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]/)) print substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); exit }
    ' "$FILE")"
    # A live plan (under grimoires/loa/, not its archive) must carry a parseable header date,
    # or the gate below would fail open; archived plans and fixtures keep the WARN.
    local canon="" root=""
    canon="$(cd "$(dirname -- "$FILE")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)/$(basename -- "$FILE")" || canon=""
    root="$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || root=""
    if [[ -z "$plan_date" && -n "$root" ]]; then
        case "$canon" in
            "${root}/grimoires/loa/archive/"*) ;;
            "${root}/grimoires/loa/"*)
                violations+=("a sprint plan carries **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD in its header (before the first '## ' heading); ${FILE} has none that parses, so the Seams gate (from ${SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM}) cannot be judged")
                return 0 ;;
        esac
    fi
    local missing
    missing="$(LC_ALL=C awk "$fence_src"'
        function emit() { if (insp && rows < 1) printf "%s (line %d)\n", head, hl }
        md_fence($0) { next }
        /^## / {
            emit(); insp = 0
            if ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/) { insp = 1; head = substr($0, 4); hl = NR; rows = 0; inseam = 0 }
            next
        }
        !insp { next }
        /^###/ { inseam = ($0 ~ /^### Seams Under Test[[:space:]]*$/); sep = 0; next }
        inseam && /^\|/ {
            if ($0 ~ /^\|[[:space:]:|-]+$/) { sep = 1 } else if (sep) { rows++ }
        }
        END { emit() }
    ' "$FILE")"
    [[ -n "$missing" ]] || return 0
    if [[ -n "$plan_date" && ! "$plan_date" < "$SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM" ]]; then
        local m
        while IFS= read -r m; do
            [[ -n "$m" ]] || continue
            violations+=("sprint block '${m}' has no '### Seams Under Test' table with at least one row: a plan dated ${plan_date} (on or after ${SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM}) needs | Seam | Catches | Misses | Prior art | per sprint — see planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md")
        done <<< "$missing"
    else
        warnings+=("${plan_date:-undated} plan: $(wc -l <<< "$missing" | tr -d ' ') sprint block(s) without a '### Seams Under Test' table; the block is required for plans dated from ${SEAMS_REQUIRED_FROM}")
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# sprint: a 'kind:' tag ends every task line (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.1; DEC-0144, DEC-0154)
# =============================================================================
# Gated on the header **Date:** exactly as the Seams rule above: from KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM
# on, every top-level '- [ ]' / '- [x]' line under '### Technical Tasks', and every
# '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside a '## Sprint N' block,
# ends with exactly one 'kind: mechanical|judgment|operator' token (whitespace around the
# colon allowed, nothing but whitespace after the value; the ⇐ dependency marker may be
# absent). Older and undated plans WARN once; a live plan without a parseable header date
# fails. Inline code spans are not tokens. A 'judgment' task that names only *.sh, *.py or
# *.ts files, or the verbs script, lint or generate, WARNs (never fails).
# @guard validator:sprint.kinds
KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM="2026-10-14"

validate_sprint_kinds() {
    local fence_src
    if ! fence_src="$(cat "${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/md-fence.awk" 2>/dev/null)" || [[ -z "$fence_src" ]]; then
        violations+=("cannot read ${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/md-fence.awk; the sprint kind: check needs it (reinstall the framework scripts)")
        return 0
    fi
    local plan_date
    plan_date="$(LC_ALL=C awk "$fence_src"'
        md_fence($0) { next }
        /^## / { exit }
        /^\*\*Date:?\*\*:?/ { if (match($0, /[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]/)) print substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); exit }
    ' "$FILE")"
    local enforce=false canon="" root=""
    if [[ -n "$plan_date" ]]; then
        [[ "$plan_date" < "$KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM" ]] || enforce=true
    else
        canon="$(cd "$(dirname -- "$FILE")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)/$(basename -- "$FILE")" || canon=""
        root="$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || root=""
        if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
            case "$canon" in
                "${root}/grimoires/loa/archive/"*) ;;
                "${root}/grimoires/loa/"*)
                    violations+=("a sprint plan carries **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD in its header (before the first '## ' heading); ${FILE} has none that parses, so the kind: rule (from ${KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM}) cannot be judged")
                    return 0 ;;
            esac
        fi
    fi
    local findings
    findings="$(LC_ALL=C awk "$fence_src"'
        function ntok(s,   n) {
            n = 0
            while (match(s, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:/)) { n++; s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH) }
            return n
        }
        md_fence($0) { next }
        /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
        !insp { next }
        /^### / {
            sec = 0
            if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
            else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
            next
        }
        !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
        sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
        {
            raw = $0; t = raw
            gsub(/`[^`]*`/, "", t)
            n = ntok(t)
            if (n == 0) { printf "M\t%d\t0\n", NR; next }
            if (n > 1) { printf "D\t%d\t%d\n", NR, n; next }
            if (raw !~ /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/) {
                if (t ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/) printf "T\t%d\t0\n", NR
                else printf "U\t%d\t0\n", NR
                next
            }
            if (raw !~ /judgment[[:space:]]*$/) next
            files = 0; code = 0; s = raw
            while (match(s, /[A-Za-z0-9_.\/*-]+\.(sh|py|ts|js|md|yaml|yml|json|tsv|bats|txt|toml)([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/)) {
                tok = substr(s, RSTART, RLENGTH); s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
                files++
                if (tok ~ /\.(sh|py|ts)([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/) code++
            }
            v = tolower(t)
            if ((files > 0 && files == code) || v ~ /(^|[^a-z0-9_])(script|lint|generate)([^a-z0-9_]|$)/) printf "J\t%d\t0\n", NR
        }
    ' "$FILE")"
    [[ -n "$findings" ]] || return 0
    local code ln extra
    local -a bad=()
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r code ln extra; do
        case "$code" in
            J) warnings+=("$FILE:$ln: a task tagged kind: judgment names only *.sh/*.py/*.ts files or the verbs script, lint, generate; if a script could do it reliably, tag it kind: mechanical") ;;
            M) bad+=("$FILE:$ln: a task line has no kind: token; end it with ' · kind: mechanical|judgment|operator'") ;;
            D) bad+=("$FILE:$ln: a task line carries ${extra} kind: tokens; keep exactly one, at the end of the line") ;;
            T) bad+=("$FILE:$ln: a task line has text after its kind: value; the kind: token ends the line") ;;
            U) bad+=("$FILE:$ln: a task line's kind: value is not one of mechanical, judgment, operator (lower case)") ;;
        esac
    done <<< "$findings"
    [[ ${#bad[@]} -gt 0 ]] || return 0
    if [[ "$enforce" == "true" ]]; then
        local b
        for b in "${bad[@]}"; do
            violations+=("${b} (a plan dated ${plan_date}, on or after ${KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM}, tags every task; see planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md)")
        done
    else
        warnings+=("${plan_date:-undated} plan: ${#bad[@]} task line(s) without a valid kind: tag; the tag is required for plans dated from ${KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM}")
    fi
}

+        md_fence($0) { next }
+        /^## / { exit }

+    ' "$FILE")"
+    local enforce=false canon="" root=""
+    if [[ -n "$plan_date" ]]; then
+        [[ "$plan_date" < "$KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM" ]] || enforce=true
+    else
+        canon="$(cd "$(dirname -- "$FILE")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)/$(basename -- "$FILE")" || canon=""
+        root="$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || root=""

+                    return 0 ;;
+            esac
+        fi
+    fi
+    local findings
+    findings="$(LC_ALL=C awk "$fence_src"'
+        function ntok(s,   n) {
+            n = 0
+            while (match(s, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:/)) { n++; s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH) }
+            return n
+        }

 `compare.sh` refuses a baseline whose `prompt_tree_sha` equals the tree under comparison, whose
 `captured_at_commit` is not a descendant of the suite's `ab.floor_commit`, or whose `corpus_sha256`
 drifted (`evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats`). Tests: `evals/tests/{execute-agent,eval-recall-grader,implement-discipline-grader,recall-baseline-freshness}.bats`.
+
+## Control arms and the record corpus (cycle-129 FR-2)
+
+Each recall suite pre-registers control arms in `ab.arms` (review: `baseline`, `no_companion`
+(informational), `no_karpathy`, `no_rule_files`; audit: `baseline`, `no_audit_delta`) and the verdict rule
+in `ab.threshold`. `execute-agent.sh` applies an arm (`LOA_EVAL_ARM`) to the sandbox copy only, after
+materialisation and immediately before the executor starts, and fails the trial (exit 2) when a toggle
+cannot take effect; `executor.json` records `arm`, `arm_toggles`, `arm_evidence`, `source_commit`,
+`models_used` and `refusal_fallbacks`. The executor never inherits the calling Claude Code session's
+coupling, and its subagent model is pinned to `EVAL_MODEL`.
+
+The record fixtures `pr-11` … `pr-18` are the round-1 states of sprints 247–254, built by
+`harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh` from `review-prs/record-pairs.tsv` and the `record/cycle-12x-a2a`
+branches. A feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit touches the file it cites. Labels
+live in the hidden `review-prs/labels/pr-NN.tsv` (never in the sandbox-copied `pr-NN/`), every drop is
+explained in `labels/pr-NN.dropped.txt`, and hand curation is the data file `labels/curation.tsv`,
+re-applied on every seed. `fix` rows (the hunks the fix commit changed) feed the grader's refuted share
+only. A label file is approved with `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve pr-NN --by "<who> <date>"`;
+`run-arms.sh` refuses unapproved fixtures unless `--allow-unapproved`.
+
+```bash
+# one suite, one batch, against a detached worktree pinned at the source commit
+./evals/harness/run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_companion,no_karpathy,no_rule_files \
+  --fixtures pr-01,pr-02,pr-03,pr-04,pr-05,pr-06,pr-07,pr-08 --trials 3 --source-commit 864069f2 --dry-run
+./evals/harness/report.sh --arms            # refuses until STATUS.json is complete; --partial for interim
+./evals/harness/compare.sh --ab --arm-a evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/baseline \
+  --arm-b evals/results/arms/review-recall/<batch>/no_karpathy --metric recall
+```
+
+Tests: `evals/tests/{arm-toggles,run-arms,arms-report,seed-corpus}.bats`.

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/recall-baseline-freshness.bats — cycle-124 Sprint 3 Task 3.2
# (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol; SDD §3.6 "compare.sh refuses drift")
#
# compare.sh freshness rule: a baseline that carries prompt_tree_sha is
# refused (exit 2) when it equals the prompt tree under comparison
# (tautological), when its captured_at_commit predates the suite's
# ab.floor_commit (stale), or when the corpus manifest hash drifted.
# --ab mode compares two arm run dirs on recall / false positives / tokens
# and refuses invalid runs (model skew, dirty trees, identical prompt trees).
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  COMPARE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/compare.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bf.XXXXXX")"
  # A prompt tree with two commits: floor (c1) and a later one (c2).
  TREE="$T/tree"; mkdir -p "$TREE/.claude"
  ( cd "$TREE" && git init -q \
    && echo a > "$TREE/.claude/a" && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m c1 \
    && echo b > "$TREE/.claude/b" && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m c2 )
  C1="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD~1)"; C2="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD)"
  TREE_SHA="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD:.claude)"
  OLD_TREE_SHA="$(git -C "$TREE" rev-parse HEAD~1:.claude)"
  # corpus manifest + suite with ab block
  mkdir -p "$T/corpus" "$T/suites"
  echo "abc  pr-01/head.diff" > "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS"
  CORPUS_SHA="$(sha256sum "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  cat > "$T/suites/rr.yaml" <<YAML
name: rr
ab:
  floor_commit: "$C1"
  corpus_manifest: "$T/corpus/SHA256SUMS"
YAML
  cat > "$T/results.jsonl" <<'JSONL'

     2	
     3	**Version:** 1.3
     4	**Date:** 2026-10-13
     5	**Author:** Sprint Planner Agent (Claude Fable 5.1, unattended)

    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## Executive Summary
    14	
    15	Three sprints deliver the eight functional requirements of the cycle-128 PRD without changing verdict derivation, gate ordering or the dissent artefact gate (the review skill gains two checklist rows and one citation line; nothing it gates changes). Sprint 1 lands the small, high-leverage changes and the decision ledger the later sprints write to. Sprint 2 builds the decision map (`/chart`) and the prototype-ticket discipline on top of the ledger. Sprint 3 adds the glossary, the seams-under-test and red-before-green checks, the documentation, and the end-to-end validation of every PRD goal. Each sprint is implemented by Opus 5.5 subagents in worktrees, reviewed and audited on Fable 5.1 with at most three dissent runs per gate, and closed through the run loop. Sequencing constraint: tasks that edit shared files (`validate-artifact.sh`, `golden-path.sh`, `settings.json`, `.gitignore`, the planning SKILL.md files) are serialised through the lead's merge of patches; independent tasks run in parallel worktrees. The lead's main checkout is the only writer of `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`; implementers and tests write fixtures only (`--file`). Evidence for every acceptance criterion lives under `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-<global>/` (implementation report `reviewer.md`, triage tables, transcripts, command output).

    18	**Sprint Duration:** 1 day each (unattended)
    19	**Estimated Completion:** 2026-10-16

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.5 (FR-2, SDD D-2.2)
     4	#
     5	# seed-corpus-from-record.sh over a tiny record tree built from
     6	# evals/tests/fixtures/seed-record/: a throwaway repo with base, head and fix
     7	# commits and a record branch carrying one round-1 review file. Proves: a
     8	# finding whose fix touches its file is kept; a finding whose file the fix
     9	# never touches is dropped by the rule; fix rows come from the fix hunks; a
    10	# finding carrying a secret is rejected; the approved-by header is required;
    11	# the labels stay out of the sandbox-copied fixture dir; SHA256SUMS covers it.
    12	# =============================================================================
    13	
    14	setup() {
    15	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    16	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    17	  SEED="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh"
    18	  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh"
    19	  FX="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/seed-record"
    20	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sc.XXXXXX")"
    21	  G="$T/repo"; C="$T/corpus"; K="$T/tasks"
    22	  mkdir -p "$G" "$C/pr-01" "$C/labels" "$K"
    23	  # the fake key is assembled here so no literal key shape is ever committed
    24	  FAKE_KEY="AKIA$(printf 'QZ%.0s' 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8)"
    25	  gc() { git -C "$G" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t "$@"; }
    26	  git -C "$G" init -q -b main
    27	  cp -R "$FX/base/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "base"
    28	  cp -R "$FX/head/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "feat: sprint-901 the input helper (round 1)"
    29	  cp -R "$FX/fix/." "$G/"; gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "fix: sprint-901 review round 1"
    30	  BASE="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD~2)"; HEAD_C="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD~1)"; FIX="$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD)"
    31	  gc checkout -q --orphan record/cycle-901-a2a
    32	  git -C "$G" rm -rq --cached . ; find "$G" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name .git -exec rm -rf {} +
    33	  mkdir -p "$G/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901"
    34	  sed "s/@SECRET@/$FAKE_KEY/" "$FX/engineer-feedback-r1.md.in" > "$G/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901/engineer-feedback-r1.md"
    35	  gc add -A; gc commit -q -m "record"; gc checkout -q main
    36	  # a minimal corpus: the instruction templates and the corpus spec header
    37	  echo "# Review instructions" > "$C/pr-01/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
    38	  echo "# Audit instructions" > "$C/pr-01/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
    39	  printf 'fixture\tkind\tcommit\tfile\tdefect_id\tseverity\tcategory\tmust_match\n' > "$C/corpus.tsv"
    40	  ARGS=(--repo "$G" --corpus "$C" --tasks-dir "$K" --base "$BASE" --head "$HEAD_C" --fix "$FIX" --feedback engineer-feedback-r1.md --out "$C/pr-90")
    41	}
    42	
    43	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    44	
    45	@test "SC-1 seeding builds the fixture; labels stay hidden; the fix-touches-file rule keeps a.sh and drops b.sh; fix rows come from the fix hunks" {
    46	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    47	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    48	  for f in fixture.yaml head.diff PR.md REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md head/scripts/a.sh head/scripts/b.sh base/scripts/a.sh; do
    49	    [ -f "$C/pr-90/$f" ]
    50	  done
    51	  grep -q '^sprint: 901$' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    52	  grep -q "^head_commit: \"$HEAD_C\"$" "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    53	  grep -q "^fix_commit: \"$FIX\"$" "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    54	  grep -q '^record_ref: "record/cycle-901-a2a"$' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    55	  grep -q 'grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-901/engineer-feedback-r1.md' "$C/pr-90/fixture.yaml"
    56	  # the labels never sit in the directory the sandbox copies
    57	  [ -z "$(find "$C/pr-90" -name 'labels*' -o -name '*.dropped.txt')" ]
    58	  L="$C/labels/pr-90.tsv"
    59	  [ "$(head -1 "$L")" = "# approved-by: pending" ]
    60	  grep -qx "$(printf 'defect_id\tseverity\tcategory\tfile\tmust_match\tlabel_source\tsource')" "$L"
    61	  # kept: the a.sh finding (its fix touches a.sh), anchored where the fix inserts
    62	  # the missing check (after `local v="$1"`) and on the short function's definition
    63	  [ "$(awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L/ {print $4 "|" $6}' "$L" | sort -u)" = "scripts/a.sh|review" ]
    64	  awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L01-/ {print $5}' "$L" | grep -qxF 'local v="$1"'
    65	  awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L01-/ {print $5}' "$L" | grep -qxF 'check_input() {'
    66	  # dropped by the rule: b.sh (the fix never touches it); the prose finding; the previous-round section is never read
    67	  grep -q 'fix commit does not touch scripts/b.sh' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    68	  grep -q 'no code locus' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    69	  ! grep -q 'must never be read' "$L" "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    70	  # fix rows: one per fix hunk, on a.sh and c.sh, sourced fix/<sha>:<start>-<end>
    71	  [ "$(awk -F'\t' '$6 == "fix" {print $4}' "$L" | sort | tr '\n' ,)" = "scripts/a.sh,scripts/c.sh," ]
    72	  awk -F'\t' '$6 == "fix" {print $7}' "$L" | grep -qE "^fix/${FIX:0:12}:[0-9]+-[0-9]+$"
    73	  # the hidden manifest, the tasks, the corpus row and the freeze
    74	  M="$C/manifests/pr-90.json"
    75	  [ "$(jq -r '.approved' "$M")" = "false" ]
    76	  [ "$(jq -r '.defects | length' "$M")" = "1" ]
    77	  [ "$(jq -r '.fix_regions | length' "$M")" = "2" ]
    78	  [ "$(jq -r '.defects[0].label_source' "$M")" = "review" ]
    79	  [ -f "$K/review-recall/review-pr-90.yaml" ] && [ -f "$K/audit-recall/audit-pr-90.yaml" ]
    80	  [ "$(yq -r '.graders[0].args[0]' "$K/review-recall/review-pr-90.yaml")" = "pr-90" ]
    81	  grep -q "^pr-90	record	${HEAD_C:0:8}	labels/pr-90.tsv" "$C/corpus.tsv"
    82	  run "$SEED" --check --corpus "$C"
    83	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    84	}
    85	
    86	@test "SC-2 a finding carrying a secret is rejected without its text; nothing written carries the key and every file passes no-secrets.sh" {
    87	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    88	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    89	  grep -q 'secret pattern in the finding text' "$C/labels/pr-90.dropped.txt"
    90	  ! grep -rqF "$FAKE_KEY" "$C"
    91	  ! awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^L/ {print $4}' "$C/labels/pr-90.tsv" | grep -q 'c.sh'
    92	  run bash "$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/no-secrets.sh" "$C"
    93	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    94	}
    95	
    96	@test "SC-3 recall-vs-defects.sh grades the seeded label: the anchor detects it, a fix region is not refuted, an unrelated line is" {
    97	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
    98	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    99	  local at; at="$(jq -r '.defects[0].anchor_line' "$C/manifests/pr-90.json")"
   100	  W="$T/ws"; mkdir -p "$W"
   101	  printf '%s\n' "- HIGH head/scripts/a.sh:$at accepts an empty value" "- LOW head/scripts/c.sh:3 prints the token" \
   102	    "- LOW head/scripts/b.sh:2 loops forever" > "$W/review.md"
   103	  EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR="$C/manifests" run "$GRADER" "$W" pr-90 review.md
   104	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   105	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.recall == 1')" = "true" ]
   106	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.findings_cited')" = "3" ]
   107	  [ "$(echo "$output" | jq -r '.details.findings_refuted')" = "1" ]
   108	}
   109	
   110	@test "SC-4 the approved-by header is required; --approve records the approver, marks the manifest approved and refreezes" {
   111	  run "$SEED" 901 record/cycle-901-a2a "${ARGS[@]}"
   112	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   113	  L="$C/labels/pr-90.tsv"
   114	  cp "$L" "$T/keep.tsv"
   115	  tail -n +2 "$T/keep.tsv" > "$L"
   116	  run "$SEED" --build-manifest pr-90 --corpus "$C"
   117	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   118	  grep -q 'approved-by' <<<"$output"
   119	  cp "$T/keep.tsv" "$L"
   120	  run "$SEED" --approve pr-90 --by "lead 2026-10-14" --corpus "$C"
   121	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   122	  [ "$(head -1 "$L")" = "# approved-by: lead 2026-10-14" ]
   123	  [ "$(jq -r '.approved' "$C/manifests/pr-90.json")" = "true" ]
   124	  [ "$(jq -r '.approved_by' "$C/manifests/pr-90.json")" = "lead 2026-10-14" ]
   125	  run "$SEED" --check --corpus "$C"
   126	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   127	  run "$SEED" --approve pr-90 --by 'x;$(id)' --corpus "$C"
   128	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   129	}
   130	
   131	@test "SC-5 curation.tsv drops or re-anchors a label on every re-seed" {
   132	  printf 'fixture\tlabel\taction\tvalue\treason\npr-90\tL01\tanchors\treturn 0\ttest re-anchor\n' > "$C/labels/curation.tsv"

# .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml — the guard origin map (cycle-129 SDD D-1.1, §3.1).
#
# The one hand-written input of the guard register. `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`
# enumerates the guards from the repository (hook commands in .claude/settings.json,
# `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, `# @guard validator:<id>`
# markers in validate-artifact.sh) and fails (exit 5) when one has no row here, when a
# row here resolves to nothing, or when a row's origin is empty. It then writes the
# tracked structural register grimoires/loa/guards.md and the untracked host yield
# .run/guard-yield.{md,json}. Regenerate after editing: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table
#
# Row fields:
#   id             hook:<path under .claude/hooks> (scripts outside it: hook:scripts/<name>),
#                  fence:<pattern id>, validator:<type>.<rule>, gate:<name>, policy:<name>;
#                  ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$
#   kind           hook | fence | validator | gate | policy
#   class          harness (the model cannot override it) | script (a script checks or
#                  reports) | prose (the model is asked to comply)
#   status         active | dormant (armed only by the env var named in knob) |
#                  telemetry (observes and logs, never refuses)
#   origin         {kind: kf|issue|finding|cycle|design, ref: <non-empty>}; design rows
#                  cite the commit that added the guard (git log --follow --diff-filter=A)
#   knob           the config key or env var that arms, relaxes or disables it, or none
#   floor          true exactly for the ids in .claude/data/floor.yaml floor_guards
#   registrations  hook rows: every "<Event>:<matcher>" (or "<Event>" when the
#                  registration has no matcher) from .claude/settings.json; [] otherwise
#   script         gate and policy rows: the file that implements it (must exist)
#   note           one line; the hooks-reference table's Purpose column for hook rows
schema_version: 1
guards:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------- hooks
  - id: hook:scripts/upgrade-health-check.sh
    kind: hook
    class: script
    status: active
    origin: {kind: design, ref: "v1.5.0 692aa617"}
    knob: none
    floor: false
    registrations: ["Setup"]
    note: "Post-install and post-upgrade health check of the framework mount"
  - id: hook:scripts/check-updates.sh
    kind: hook
    class: script
    status: active
    origin: {kind: design, ref: "v0.14.0 1f448140"}
    knob: update_check.enabled
    floor: false
    registrations: ["SessionStart"]
    note: "Notify when a newer framework release exists (cached; LOA_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=1 silences it)"
  - id: hook:session-start/loa-l6-surface-handoffs.sh
    kind: hook
    class: script
    status: active
    origin: {kind: cycle, ref: "cycle-098 FR-L6 (#771)"}
    knob: structured_handoff.enabled
    floor: false
    registrations: ["SessionStart"]
    note: "Surface unread L6 structured handoffs inside a data fence"
  - id: hook:session-start/loa-l7-surface-soul.sh
    kind: hook
    class: script

   161	# The arm's toggles: explicit JSON, else the suite's ab.arms[] entry.
   162	resolve_toggles() {
   163	  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES:-}" ]]; then
   164	    jq -ce 'if type == "object" then . else error("not an object") end' <<<"$LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES" 2>/dev/null \
   165	      || { echo "ERROR: LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES is not a JSON object" >&2; return 2; }
   166	    return 0
   167	  fi
   168	  local suite_file="${LOA_EVAL_SUITE_FILE:-}"
   169	  if [[ -z "$suite_file" ]]; then
   170	    local tdir; tdir="$(basename "$(dirname "$TASK_YAML")")"
   171	    [[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/$tdir.yaml" ]] && suite_file="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/$tdir.yaml"
   172	  fi
   173	  local t="" found=0
   174	  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
   175	    found="$(ARM="$ARM" yq '[.ab.arms[]? | select(.id == strenv(ARM))] | length' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
   176	    [[ "$found" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || found=0
   177	    if [[ "$found" -gt 0 ]]; then
   178	      t="$(ARM="$ARM" yq -o=json -I=0 '[.ab.arms[] | select(.id == strenv(ARM))][0].toggles // {}' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)"
   179	    fi
   180	  fi
   181	  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 || -z "$t" || "$t" == "null" ]]; then
   182	    [[ "$ARM" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; }
   183	    echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' is not declared in ${suite_file:-any suite} (ab.arms[])" >&2
   184	    return 2
   185	  fi
   186	  printf '%s' "$t"
   187	}
   188	ARM_TOGGLES="$(resolve_toggles)" || exit 2

   190	# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
   191	# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
   192	_drop_md_section() {
   193	  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmp
   194	  tmp="$(mktemp "$eval_dir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
   195	  awk -v h="$heading" '
   196	    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
   197	    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
   198	    skip { n++; next }
   199	    { print }
   200	    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
   201	  mv "$tmp" "$f"
   202	  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
   203	}
   204	
   205	# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
   206	# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
   207	# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
   208	_drop_paragraph() {
   209	  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
   210	import re, sys
   211	path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   212	text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
   213	paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
   214	for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
   215	    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
   216	        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
   217	            removed = paras[i]
   218	            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
   219	            del paras[i:i + 2]
   220	            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
   221	            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
   222	            sys.exit(0)
   223	sys.exit(1)
   224	PY
   225	}
   226	
   227	ARM_EVIDENCE='{}'
   228	_evidence() { ARM_EVIDENCE="$(jq -c --arg k "$1" --arg v "$2" '. + {($k): $v}' <<<"$ARM_EVIDENCE")"; }
   229	
   230	apply_toggles() {
   231	  local key val
   232	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
   233	    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
   234	    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
   235	      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
   236	    fi
   237	    case "$key" in
   238	      companion_voice)
   239	        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
   240	        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
   241	        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
   242	          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
   243	        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
   244	          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
   245	        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
   246	        ;;
   247	      karpathy_block)
   248	        local k="$WORKSPACE/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
   249	        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md" >&2; return 2; }
   250	        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"
   251	        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
   252	          echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed" >&2; return 2
   253	        fi
   254	        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json"
   255	        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
   256	          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" && mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
   257	        fi
   258	        _evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md"
   259	        ;;
   260	      rule_files)
   261	        local r gone=""
   262	        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
   263	          if [[ -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
   264	          [[ ! -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: $r still present" >&2; return 2; }
   265	        done
   266	        _evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
   267	        ;;
   268	      audit_delta_instruction)
   269	        local s="$WORKSPACE/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
   270	        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
   271	        _drop_paragraph "$s" "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" \
   272	          || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
   273	        _evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
   274	        ;;
   275	      *) echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' declares unknown toggle '$key'" >&2; return 2 ;;
   276	    esac
   277	  done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$ARM_TOGGLES")
   278	  return 0
   279	}
   280	apply_toggles || exit 2

not ok 1 SC-1 seeding builds the fixture; labels stay hidden; the fix-touches-file rule keeps a.sh and drops b.sh; fix rows come from the fix hunks
not ok 2 SC-2 a finding carrying a secret is rejected without its text; nothing written carries the key and every file passes no-secrets.sh
not ok 3 SC-3 recall-vs-defects.sh grades the seeded label: the anchor detects it, a fix region is not refuted, an unrelated line is
not ok 4 SC-4 the approved-by header is required; --approve records the approver, marks the manifest approved and refreezes
not ok 5 SC-5 curation.tsv drops or re-anchors a label on every re-seed
not ok 6 SC-6 --dry-run writes nothing; a missing commit, a missing record ref and a non-record fixture are refused
not ok 7 RG-1 exact anchor with head/ prefix is detected; recall is detected/planted
not ok 8 RG-2 a citation 3 lines away counts, 4 lines away does not
not ok 9 RG-3 a line range covering the anchor counts
not ok 10 RG-4 basename-only and repo-relative citations both match the manifest file
not ok 11 RG-5 a different file at the anchor line is not a detection
not ok 12 RG-6 clean fixture: false positives come from the trailer's critical+high; zero passes

}

# Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

## Agent type tool allowlists

| Agent type | Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | Use for |
|------------|-----------------------------|---------|
| `general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork` | ✓ all tools | Skills that author files |
| `Plan` | ✗ excluded | Read-only planning / exploration |
| `Explore` | ✗ excluded | Read-only codebase analysis |
| `loa-scout`, `prompt-auditor`, `prompt-auditor-io` | ✗ excluded | Read-only project agents (`.claude/agents/`) |
| (unset) | inherited from caller | Default; safe for write-capable skills |

Source: Claude Code agent-type definitions in the system prompt, and `.claude/agents/*.md`.

## Enforcement

`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:

> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …

The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.

## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)

`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application
code outside `/implement`") mechanical for review skills rather than prose-only.

| Skill class | `disallowed-tools` | Why |
|-------------|--------------------|-----|
| Pure-review (`write_files: false`, no report artifacts) | `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | Never writes anything — remove the write tools outright |
| Sprint review/audit (`reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit` | Write STATE-zone feedback/checkmarks/COMPLETED markers, run the allowed verdict check and run `adversarial-review.sh` (forks the provider CLIs, appends the `.run` cost and MODELINV ledgers, moves the previous round's a2a envelope aside as `.prev`, writes the new one; review also runs `qmd-context-query.sh`); System remains `none` and App remains `read` |
| Report-authoring review (`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit`, `Bash(git add/commit/push *)` | Legitimately write STATE-zone reports/vision/lore, so `Write` is retained; app-code prevention is governed by **zones**, and the implementation-only git mutations are removed |

**`REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS`** (in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`):
`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`, `spiraling`, `autonomous-agent`,
`run-bridge`, `run-mode`, `reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`. These `role: review` skills keep `Write` by design —
the adversarial/report authors write STATE-zone artifacts, and the autonomous
orchestrators dispatch implementation through the harness (which runs inside
`/implement`, where writes are sanctioned). The validator emits a WARN for any *other* `role: review`
skill that declares `write_files: true` without disallowing `Write` — surfacing
a new C-PROC-001 gap at lint time. `disallowed-tools` is tool-granular, not
path-granular; it cannot express "no `src/` writes but yes `grimoires/` writes",
which is why report-authoring skills rely on zones for path-level control.

## Scope

Applies to every `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`. The lint runs as part of the normal validation suite (`bats tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats`).

## Origin

- Defect: [#553](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/553) — `/architect` and `/sprint-plan` produced correct output but refused to write their target files. Three independent reproductions across two repos.
- Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557) — Tier 1 cycle-083 framework boundary fixes.
- Sprint: `sprint-bug-102` — test-first patch landing the invariant lint + the three frontmatter fixes.

## Related rules

- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` is framework-managed; SKILL.md edits require cycle-level authorization.
- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — file-creation safety when authoring SKILL.md via heredoc.

# Git Stash Safety

`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.

**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.

## The safe interface

```bash
source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
```

Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):

```bash
worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
```

## Judgment rules the fence cannot express

- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.

## Origin

- Defect: [#555](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/555) — 4 Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost to the hazard pattern; recovered only because `git gc --prune=now` hadn't run. Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557).
- The hazard shape recurred live during cycle-122 itself (a `git stash pop >/dev/null 2>&1` during a baseline check — caught, verified lossless, and turned into the FR-1.2b fence the same day).

## Related rules

- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — heredoc safety, strict-mode patterns.
- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` framework boundary (Bash writes now fenced by FR-SZ2).

     3	# evals/tests/arms-report.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
     4	#
     5	# report.sh --arms over a fixture results tree (the layout run-arms.sh
     6	# writes): the pre-registered verdicts, the bootstrap interval, refuted share,
     7	# missed labels, the refusal while STATUS.json is not complete and the
     8	# --partial header. Thresholds come from the real review-recall suite.

    10	
    11	setup() {

    19	          model_id:"claude-fable-5-1", arms:["baseline","no_companion","no_karpathy","no_rule_files"], fixtures:["pr-01","pr-02","pr-03"], trials:3}' \

    32	row() {

     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD AC-1.5, SDD §1.6, D-9.2)
     5	# The floor does not move: every floor_files entry of .claude/data/floor.yaml
     6	# and the fence-corpus rows named under floor_corpus are byte-identical to
     7	# origin/main; the register disables nothing, so the .claude/settings.json hook
     8	# registrations and the fence's pattern-id call-site list are identical too.

    10	# checkout); the floor.yaml sha256 pin in guard-origins.bats still runs there.
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	setup() {

    18	    skip "origin/main is not reachable from this checkout (shallow clone?): the floor snapshot needs it — run 'git fetch origin main'"
    19	  fi

    23	base_show() { git -C "$ROOT" show "$BASE:$1"; }

    33	  [ "$n" -ge 4 ]

     5	# execute-agent.sh applies a control arm's toggles to the sandbox copy only.

     8	# prompt at the moment it starts (STUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR), after every
     9	# materialisation step. The arm ids and toggles come from the real suite
    10	# files; the prompt tree is a synthetic fixture so later prose edits to the
    11	# live kernel cannot change what this test proves.

# .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml — the guard origin map (cycle-129 SDD D-1.1, §3.1).
#
# The one hand-written input of the guard register. `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh`
# enumerates the guards from the repository (hook commands in .claude/settings.json,
# `# @guard fence:<id>` markers in block-destructive-bash.sh, `# @guard validator:<id>`
# markers in validate-artifact.sh) and fails (exit 5) when one has no row here, when a
# row here resolves to nothing, or when a row's origin is empty. It then writes the
# tracked structural register grimoires/loa/guards.md and the untracked host yield
# .run/guard-yield.{md,json}. Regenerate after editing: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table
#
# Row fields:
#   id             hook:<path under .claude/hooks> (scripts outside it: hook:scripts/<name>),
#                  fence:<pattern id>, validator:<type>.<rule>, gate:<name>, policy:<name>;
#                  ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$
#   kind           hook | fence | validator | gate | policy
#   class          harness (the model cannot override it) | script (a script checks or
#                  reports) | prose (the model is asked to comply)
#   status         active | dormant (armed only by the env var named in knob) |
