7:**Beads**: The local-first task tracker, driven through its br command, that is the single source of truth for sprint tasks, decision tickets and their dependencies.
10:**Bridgebuilder**: The automated pull-request reviewer that posts findings on a pull request and drives the iterative improvement loop of a bridge run.
12:**Cheval**: The model-dispatch substrate through which every call to an external model provider is routed, with fallback, budget limits and cost accounting.
14:**Circuit breaker**: The run-mode guard that halts a run after repeated identical findings, no progress, a cycle limit or a timeout, leaving the run for the operator to resume.
16:**Construct**: An installable package of skills, personas and grimoire paths that extends the framework for a domain and may declare its own workflow gates.
18:**DEC row**: One entry of the decision ledger, numbered DEC-NNNN, recording a decision, its alternatives, its status and the voice that proposed or decided it.
21:**Decision ticket**: A question-type bead under a map epic whose resolution is a decision, not a build slice.
24:**decision:grilling**: The label of a decision ticket that talking can settle, answered in interview rounds with the operator.
26:**decision:prototype**: The label of a decision ticket the operator needs to see before answering, settled by a spike and its verdict.
28:**decision:research**: The label of a decision ticket that needs reading or sources, answered by a read-only research report and one confirming round.
30:**decision:unblock**: The label of a decision ticket that a read-only probe settles by showing whether a suspected blocker is real; it never builds anything.
32:**Dissent**: A second model's independent review of the same diff, triaged before a gate verdict.
35:**Flatline**: The multi-model adversarial review of planning documents, in which independent voices review and cross-score each other before findings are integrated.
38:**Fog of war**: Decisions an effort can tell are coming but cannot yet phrase sharply; a map keeps them under Not yet specified.
40:**Frontier**: The open, unblocked, unclaimed decision tickets of a map; in an interview, the questions whose prerequisites are already settled.
42:**Golden path**: The five everyday commands (loa, plan, build, review and ship) that detect where the workflow stands and route to the right truename.
44:**Grimoire**: The project's state area of planning documents, notes, reviews and records that agents read and write across sessions.
46:**ICE**: Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics, the git safety layer of run mode that owns branch creation, push decisions and the refusal to touch protected branches.
48:**Implement gate**: The hook that asks before an edit to application code made outside the implement or bug workflows.
50:**Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
53:**Judgment**: The task kind for work that needs reading and a decision; it ships as prose or a reviewed artifact, and its sprint task line ends with kind: judgment.
55:**Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
58:**Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
60:**Kind counts**: The release-notes line that counts a cycle's sprint tasks by kind (mechanical, judgment and operator), read from the tagged task lines of its sprint plan.
62:**Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
65:**Lore**: The mythic and narrative background of the framework's names, kept apart from this glossary, which defines only working meanings.
67:**Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
69:**Mechanical**: The task kind for work a script could do reliably; it ships as code with tests, and a review flags a mechanical task delivered as prose the model re-executes.
71:**Operator**: The human who owns the project and its decisions; as a task kind, work that belongs to that human, which a review flags when it was completed unattended without a decision:unblock ticket or a DEC row.
73:**Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
75:**Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
78:**Seam**: A point where a test observes the system, declared in a sprint plan together with what it catches, what it misses and its prior art.
80:**Spike**: A throwaway prototype on its own branch that answers one decision ticket; only its report and its verdict row reach the working branch.
82:**Truename**: The underlying command that a golden-path command routes to, used directly by power users.
84:**Verdict trailer**: The machine-readable last line of a review or audit feedback document, which must agree with its findings. Any critical or high finding forces a changes-required verdict.
87:**Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.
89:**Volume ratio**: The release-notes line that sets a cycle's script lines changed against its prose bytes changed and its model calls; the model-call count is local to the host that ran the cycle.
91:**Zone**: One of the three permission regions of a repository: the System zone holds the framework and is never edited by hand, the State zone is read and written freely, and the App zone needs confirmation before a write.
# Glossary: Loa framework

The shared language of the Loa agent framework, for humans and agents. It is mounted into every project with the framework and defines what each word means in day-to-day work; the mythic background of the names lives in the lore, and a project's own terms belong in that project's root glossary, never here.

## Language

**Beads**: The local-first task tracker, driven through its br command, that is the single source of truth for sprint tasks, decision tickets and their dependencies.
_Aliases_: br

**Bridgebuilder**: The automated pull-request reviewer that posts findings on a pull request and drives the iterative improvement loop of a bridge run.

**Cheval**: The model-dispatch substrate through which every call to an external model provider is routed, with fallback, budget limits and cost accounting.

**Circuit breaker**: The run-mode guard that halts a run after repeated identical findings, no progress, a cycle limit or a timeout, leaving the run for the operator to resume.

**Construct**: An installable package of skills, personas and grimoire paths that extends the framework for a domain and may declare its own workflow gates.

**DEC row**: One entry of the decision ledger, numbered DEC-NNNN, recording a decision, its alternatives, its status and the voice that proposed or decided it.
_Avoid_: ADR, decision note

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# recall-vs-defects.sh — deterministic planted-defect recall grader
#
# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9). Args: $1=workspace, $2=fixture id (pr-NN),
# $3=review file (default review.md). Reads the HIDDEN manifest
# evals/fixtures/review-prs/manifests/<id>.json (never copied into the
# sandbox) and the agent's review.
#
# Rule (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol, no fuzzy adjudication): a defect is DETECTED
# when the review contains a `path:line` (or `path:line-line`) citation whose
# path ends with the defect's file (repo-relative, `head/`-prefixed, or the
# bare basename) and whose line, or line range, falls within ±3 of the
# manifest anchor — `anchor_line`, or any line in `anchors[]` for a defect
# with more than one site.
#
# Parser (1.1.0, bd-ewrc): a leading `(` is not part of the path; comma
# continuations (`path:776,807`, `path:10, 118-121`) and a later bare `:N` or
# `head:N` / `base:N` bind to the most recent cited path. A `:N` glued to a
# word or a number (`note:40`, `10:40`), or with no cited path before it,
# credits nothing.
#
# Parser 1.1.1 (sprint-250 review run 1, n40-n42): the LOA-VERDICT trailer is
# removed before citations are parsed, and a bare `:N` after a quote, bracket,
# brace or `*` (JSON such as `"high":3`) credits nothing; a backtick- or
# bold-wrapped path (`` `b.sh`:40 ``, `**b.sh**:40`) binds its own line; a comma
# continuation or range stays on its line, and a continuation must end at a
# number boundary (no dates);
# a path containing `//` (a URL) is not a citation.
# Run 2 (#11/#13-#15): a match inside any URL token (`scheme://...`) is not a
# citation; a range dash is unspaced and every number (first, continuation,
# bare) ends at a boundary (no further `-N` / `–N`: no dates); the
# quote/bracket guard applies only to the fully bare `:N` (plus a closing
# backtick), so `"head:40"` binds as in 1.1.0; one trailer pattern strips and
# reads the LOA-VERDICT comment and never crosses another comment's bounds.
# Parser 1.1.2 (the run 2 changes above, plus sprint-250 review run 3): the
# URL look-back takes the text after the last whitespace — one linear split —
# so a citation that opens a line never inherits the previous line's URL.
# The parser runs as `python3 -I -` (audit dissent run 1, n32): a module planted
# in the invoker's cwd (a forging json.py) is never imported (RG-27).
#
# Grader 1.2.0 (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.3): adds the refuted-share figure;
# the recall rule and the pass/score contract are unchanged. A FINDING is one
# distinct cited (path, line-range); it is MATCHED when it overlaps (±3) a
# defect site or a manifest `fix_regions[]` entry ({file, start, end}: the
# head-side lines a record fixture's fix commit touched). details gain
# findings_cited, findings_refuted and refuted_share (refuted / cited; null
# when nothing is cited).
#
# Clean fixtures (0 planted defects) measure FALSE POSITIVES: the LOA-VERDICT
# trailer's critical+high counts; without a trailer, every file:line citation
# counts as one.
#
# Output: {"pass", "score", "details":{recall, planted, detected[], missed[],
#          false_positives, severity_counts, model, effort, tokens}, "grader_version"}
#   pass  = every planted defect detected (defect fixture) / zero false
#           positives (clean fixture); score = recall*100 or 100/0.
# Exit: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 error (missing manifest / bad args)

ARM_EVIDENCE='{}'
_evidence() { ARM_EVIDENCE="$(jq -c --arg k "$1" --arg v "$2" '. + {($k): $v}' <<<"$ARM_EVIDENCE")"; }

apply_toggles() {
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
    if [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)" >&2; return 2
    fi
    case "$key" in
      companion_voice)
        local cfg="$WORKSPACE/.loa.config.yaml"
        [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
        yq -i '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice = false | .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice = false' "$cfg" \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle: yq failed on the sandbox config" >&2; return 2; }
        [[ "$(yq -r '.flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice' "$cfg")" == "false" ]] \
          || { echo "ERROR: companion_voice toggle did not take effect" >&2; return 2; }
        _evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
        ;;
      karpathy_block)
        local k="$WORKSPACE/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md" >&2; return 2; }
        n="$(_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles')"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
          echo "ERROR: karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed" >&2; return 2
        fi
        local cj="$WORKSPACE/.claude/data/constraints.json"
        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" && mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
        fi
        _evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md"
        ;;
      rule_files)
        local r gone=""
        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
          if [[ -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
          [[ ! -e "$WORKSPACE/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: $r still present" >&2; return 2; }
        done
        _evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
        ;;
      audit_delta_instruction)
        local s="$WORKSPACE/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
        _drop_paragraph "$s" "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" \
          || { echo "ERROR: audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md" >&2; return 2; }
        _evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
        ;;
      *) echo "ERROR: arm '$ARM' declares unknown toggle '$key'" >&2; return 2 ;;
    esac
  done < <(jq -r 'to_entries[] | [.key, (.value | tostring)] | @tsv' <<<"$ARM_TOGGLES")
  return 0
}

I found 4 high-confidence defects, 4 medium and 4 low-confidence or low-impact ones. The three new or changed test files pass in a scratch copy (`~/scratch/rev2`; `/tmp` is mounted noexec here, and I added a stub `no-secrets.sh` because the real one isn't in the snapshot). I confirmed the test defects by experiment: I broke `SKIP_SECTION` in the script and SC-1 still passed.

### High confidence

1. **head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:69, 90, 91, 143: these `! cmd` assertions can never fail.** Bash `set -e` and bats' ERR trap both ignore a command negated with `!`, unless it is the last line of the test. None of these four is last, so they check nothing:
   - 69: "previous-round section is never read"
   - 90: the fake key appears nowhere
   - 91: c.sh got no label
   - 143: no `pr-90` row left in corpus.tsv

   With `SKIP_SECTION` broken, "must never be read" shows up in `pr-90.dropped.txt` and SC-1 still reports ok. Fix: use `run ! …` or `[ "$(…)" = "" ]` style checks.

2. **head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:79, 141, 154: `[ a ] && [ b ] && …` chains only check the last test.** `set -e` does not fire when a command fails before the final `&&`. So:
   - 79 never checks that `review-pr-90.yaml` exists (line 80's `yq` partly covers it).
   - 141 only checks the review task file. It never checks that `pr-90/`, `labels/pr-90.tsv` or `manifests/pr-90.json` were removed.
   - 154 only checks `manifests`; the `pr-90` dir and the label file go unchecked.

3. **head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:159-161: SC-6's "non-record fixture is refused" case never reaches the refusal.** The test's `$C/pr-01` has no `fixture.yaml`, so the guard at seed-corpus-from-record.sh:295 is skipped.
   - The script then deletes `pr-01` (line 730), including its instruction templates.
   - It then crashes with `FileNotFoundError` copying those same templates (lines 743-745).
   - Exit 1 and the missing `fixture.yaml` make the test pass for the wrong reason. Reproduced: afterwards `pr-01/` holds only `PR.md`, `head.diff`, `base/` and `head/`.

4. **head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:769-774: when the no-secrets scan fails, the corpus is left inconsistent.** The previous good fixture dir was already deleted at line 730. The failure path then removes only `pr-NN/` and the two label files. It leaves in place:
   - the previous `manifests/pr-NN.json`
   - both task yamls
   - the `corpus.tsv` record row
   - a `SHA256SUMS` listing files that no longer exist (so `--check` fails)

   The no-labels branch (710-728) takes care to leave nothing stale; this path does not, despite saying "nothing kept".

### Medium confidence

5. **seed-corpus-from-record.sh:295 and 730: the overwrite guard only fires when `fixture.yaml` exists.** Any `pr-NN` dir without `fixture.yaml` gets deleted, and nothing refuses `fx == pr-01`, the template source at line 743. Seeding into it destroys the templates, as in finding 3.

6. **seed-corpus-from-record.sh:310-312: renamed binaries are not excluded.** `git diff --numstat -M` prints renames in brace form (`d/{a => b}/img.bin`). `p.split(" => ")[-1].strip("{}")` gives `b}/img.bin`, so the binary-exclusion check at line 321 misses it. The binary is then written into `head/` through `redact()`, which decodes with "replace" and re-encodes, corrupting it. Verified with git. Related: without `-z`, non-ASCII paths come back quoted (`"caf\303\251.sh"`), so `show()` returns None and the file silently drops out of the fixture.

7. **seed-corpus-from-record.sh:418-460 against the header at 37-39: the code doesn't follow the documented label rule.** The header says bridgebuilder findings come from "the Fixed table only", and that review sources are `engineer-feedback*` / `reviewer*`. In the code:
   - `parse_findings` never uses its `name` argument.
   - Bullet and `### [SEV]` findings in bridgebuilder files become labels.
   - The Fixed table is parsed in every feedback file.
   - `source_kind` (411-416) labels any other filename as `review`.

8. **seed-corpus-from-record.sh:586-590: the snippet narrowing can never take effect.** Lines 586-589 narrow multiple hits to the cited symbol or a ±40-line window. Line 590 then also requires `sum(1 for l in lines if s in l) == 1`, meaning the snippet must be unique in the whole file. A snippet that appears on several lines can therefore never become an anchor, unlike what the comment at 574-576 says.

### Low confidence / low impact

9. **head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-kind-01.yml:6-9.** It claims the `.yml` extension keeps the task out of every run. That holds for suites, but `run-eval.sh --skill reviewing-code` and the default all-tasks mode both pick up `*.yml` (run-eval.sh:198, 283).

10. **head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:54-55.** The Output doc was not updated with `findings_cited`, `findings_refuted` and `refuted_share`. The missing-review output at line 83 also lacks these fields.

11. **head/evals/suites/review-recall.yaml and audit-recall.yaml, `threshold` blocks.** `coverage_required`, `bootstrap.method` and `bootstrap.resample` are "pre-registered" but no code reads them (`arms-report.py` only prints `method` and `resample`). Changing them has no effect.

12. **head/evals/README.md:509-510.** It says a toggle that "cannot take effect" fails the trial with exit 2. But the `rule_files` toggle in execute-agent.sh (lines 260-266) succeeds with "none present" when neither rule file exists, so the arm silently becomes a no-op.

Not a defect, just noting: the 16 task yamls (pr-11 to pr-18) are internally consistent (ids, fixture paths, grader args), but their fixtures, manifests, `corpus.tsv` rows and `record-pairs.tsv` are not in this diff, so I couldn't check that they exist.

content.text:
I found 12 defects in the scoped files: 3 high confidence, 6 medium, 3 low. I ran the new bats files from a copy in `$HOME/rev1`, because `/tmp` is mounted noexec on this box and nothing in a `/tmp` copy can be executed. `arm-toggles.bats` and `arms-report.bats` pass in full. `execute-agent.bats` passes apart from EA-2, EA-8 and EA-9, which fail only because `head/` doesn't contain the unchanged repo files they need. `run-arms.bats` can't run at all: the `review-prs` corpus, `sandbox.sh` and `grade.sh` aren't in `head/`. So the `run-arms.sh` findings come from reading the code.

**High confidence**

1. `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:302` — The "too small to name" check uses `abs(drop) <= base_spread`. The docstring (lines 20–23) says the arm is a recall loss only when "the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread". With `abs()`, an arm that recalls *more* than baseline can be labelled `recall loss`. I reproduced it: baseline 0.5 on every trial, arm trial means 0.2/1.0/1.0 (mean 0.733, drop −0.233). Only the min-trial rule is violated, and the report says **recall loss**. It should be `drop <= base_spread`. This spread escape also isn't in the pre-registered rule in `evals/suites/review-recall.yaml` ("a violated condition reads `recall loss`").

2. `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:263-266` — The `rule_files` toggle succeeds even when neither `stash-safety.md` nor `skill-invariants.md` exists in the sandbox. It records `removed: none present` and exits 0, so the arm runs exactly as baseline. The header (lines 64–66) promises "a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)". The other three toggles do fail in this case.

3. `head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:132, 133, 152, 153, 166` — These `! grep -q …` assertions are not the last command in their tests. Bash ignores `set -e` for negated commands, so they can never fail. I confirmed with bats 1.13 that `! true` followed by `true` passes. AT-5 (Karpathy text gone), AT-7 (delta paragraph gone from the SKILL.md and system prompt) and AT-8 therefore don't check their main claims. Use `run ! grep` or `! grep … || false`. The `!` lines in `arms-report.bats` (65, 115) are last in their tests, so they do work.

**Medium confidence**

4. `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:251-257` (with 265 and 408) — Reusing a batch is allowed whenever source and model match, but there is no resume logic:
   - the full plan runs again and rows are appended (`>>`) to the existing `results.jsonl`, so trial numbers repeat;
   - the per-batch STATUS counters restart at 0;
   - `MANIFEST.json` is overwritten, possibly with different `--arms`/`--fixtures`. `arms-report.py` then ignores old arms that are no longer listed, while still counting their duplicated rows.
   
   Old error rows and duplicate trials end up mixed into the verdict.

5. `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:327` (with `verify_corpus` at 134–155) — Each trial is checked against the *current* `SHA256SUMS`. `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve`/`--build-manifest` calls `freeze()`, which rewrites `SHA256SUMS`. So relabelling or approving the fixture under test mid-batch passes the check, and that trial is graded against different labels. The change shows up only in `corpus_sha256_at_trial`, although line 17 says "a drift stops the batch". The check should compare against the digests from batch start.

6. `head/evals/harness/compare-ab.py:71-73` and `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:144-146` — Every model with output in `models_used` now counts as model skew. But `execute-agent.sh:411-413` already says haiku helper calls show up in `modelUsage`. `execute-agent.sh:349` pins only `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, not the CLI's small/fast helper model, despite the comment at 343–344 ("pin every auxiliary model"). Any trial with a helper call would therefore make an A/B invalid (exit 2) and every arm inconclusive. This is a regression for A/B runs that used to be valid.

7. `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:314` — The transport-failure heuristic greps both stderr and `agent-output.json` (the result event, which can include the model's final text) for broad terms such as `network` and `5[0-9][0-9] `. A non-transport agent failure (executor exit 1) whose text matches gets retried and recorded as `transport_error`.

8. `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:244-249` (with 426) — Cleanup on interrupt or drift kills only the `run_trial` subshells (`jobs -p`). Their `execute-agent.sh`/`timeout`/`claude` children keep running as orphans and keep using quota and writing into sandboxes. Also, background jobs ignore SIGINT when job control is off.

9. `head/evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub.sh:20` and `head/evals/tests/run-arms.bats:58` — RA-1 claims "without a … CLI call", but `run-arms.sh:171` (`write_manifest`) runs `$claude_bin --version` even in dry-run mode. I found six defects in the focus files, two of them confirmed by running the code. I ran the tests in a scratch copy under `/workspace/.eval/tmp/rev3`, because `/tmp` is mounted noexec. The PR tree only contains the changed files, so I stubbed `lib/md-fence.awk` and `compat-lib.sh`. With those stubs, all 11 KINDS tests and all 6 CR tests pass.

### Findings

1. **`head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39-41`** — FS-2 can never fail (high confidence, reproduced). The jq filter uses `$in` inside `def m(...)`, but `$in` is only bound afterwards (`. as $in | select(m($rules))`). jq scopes variables lexically, so the filter fails to compile ("$in is not defined", exit 3) on both sides. The `diff <(…) <(…)` then compares two empty streams and passes. I built a repo with an `origin/main` ref, changed an `FR-SZ-TEE` row in `corpus.jsonl`, and FS-2 still reported `ok`. The fix is to bind `. as $in` before the def, or pass `.rule` into `m`.

2. **`head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:158-159`** — the new `guard-yield.sh --check` step will fail in CI (medium-high confidence). In `--check` mode the script exits 1 when `grimoires/loa/guards.md` does not exist (`guard-yield.sh:422`: `[[ ! -f "$OUT" ]] || ! cmp …` sets drift). The PR adds `guard-yield.sh` as a new file but never commits the "tracked" register `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, and that path is not gitignored. Only the `hooks-reference.md` table was regenerated.

3. **`head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:23-46` and `:49-72`** — the `paths:` filters were not extended for the new inputs (high confidence). These are missing:
   - `tools/cycle-ratio.sh`: only `tools/modelinv-rollup.sh` and `tools/check-no-swallowed-jq.sh` are listed (lines 37-38 / 63-64).
   - `.claude/rules/**`, which `rule-paths.bats` covers.
   - `.claude/data/floor.yaml` and `.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml`: only `.claude/data/schemas/**` is listed. `guard-origins.yaml` is described as "the one hand-written input" of the drift gate.
   - `.claude/loa/**`: the generated hooks table that `--check` compares.
   - `grimoires/loa/guards.md`.
   - `.claude/skills/planning-sprints/**`: the template that KINDS-11 and SEAMS-10 pin.

   A PR that edits only these files skips the drift gate and the new suites.

4. **`head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:17-19`** with **`head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:90`** — the floor snapshot is never enforced in CI (medium confidence). The checkout uses the default `fetch-depth: 1`. On `pull_request` events `origin/main` does not exist, so FS-1 to FS-4 always skip. On `push` to main, `origin/main` is HEAD itself, so the comparison is trivially equal. Combined with finding 1, nothing in CI checks the floor files.

5. **`head/tests/unit/validate-artifact-sprint-kinds.bats:131`** — the KINDS-9 skip condition does not match `KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM=2026-10-14` (medium confidence). It runs for any date matching `2026-1[0-2]-`. A live plan dated 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-13 is pre-rule, so the validator correctly emits the "without a valid kind: tag" WARN, and line 134 then fails the test. The skip message says such plans are skipped. Plans dated 2027 or later are skipped forever.

6. **`head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:10-11`** — the comment says "Both bats suites pin this file's sha256 … (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant)". Only `guard-origins.bats:16` has the pin; `floor-snapshot.bats` has none and its own header (line 10) says so (high confidence, doc mismatch). The pinned hash does match the file.

### Lower-confidence notes

- **`head/.claude/skills/planning-sprints/resources/templates/sprint-template.md:99-118`** — the template's `### Task N.E2E` section has no `- [ ] Task N.E2E: … · kind: …` line. The validator (`validate-artifact.sh:1013`) and KINDS-8 both expect the E2E task to carry a kind tag, so plans written from the template never tag it, and the check passes silently. Low-medium confidence.
- **`head/tests/unit/cycle-ratio.bats:112-116`** — CR-6 is named "a plan with no task lines counts zero", but its plan has one task line (`kind: operator`). The zero-task case is never tested. Low severity.
- **`head/tools/cycle-ratio.sh:13-14,100`** — the comment claims "the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces". A line with two `kind:` tokens, which the validator rejects as D, is counted here under the trailing value. Low confidence.

The other focus files looked correct: the validator kinds logic beyond its tests, `display_guards_line`, the rule `paths:` globs, the `.gitignore` negation, the GLOSSARY entries (they pass `--type glossary`), the floor and validator marker sets (they match `guard-origins.yaml`), and the PB-10 constants test. The `implementing-tasks` app-zone change (read to read-write) matches that skill's own body text.

#
# Label rule: a feedback finding becomes a label only when the fix commit
# touches the file it cites (`git diff --name-only head..fix`) and that file
# is part of the fixture; label_source is review (engineer-feedback*,
# reviewer*), audit (auditor-sprint-feedback*) or bridgebuilder
# (bridgebuilder*, the "Fixed" table only). The anchor is a head-side line
# the fix changed near the cited line or inside the cited symbol; a finding
# that cites only a file is anchored on that file's fix hunks when there are
# at most four, else dropped. `fix` rows cover every hunk fix_commit changed
LATER_ROUND = re.compile(r"^#{2,4}\s+(?:\d+\.\s+)?.*\brun, on the round-", re.I)
PRE_EXISTING = re.compile(r"\bpre-?existing\b|not this sprint'?s", re.I)
TICK = re.compile(r"`([^`\n]{2,200})`")
PATHLIKE = re.compile(r"^(?:head/|base/)?[\w./+-]*[\w-]\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}(?:$|[:\s])")
BARE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w/.`-])((?:\.claude|\.github|tools|tests|evals|lib|src)/[\w./+-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})(?::(\d+(?:-\d+)?(?:,\s*\d+)*|[A-Za-z_][\w.]*))?")

def source_kind(name):
    if name.startswith("auditor"):
        return "audit"
    if name.startswith("bridgebuilder"):
        return "bridgebuilder"
    return "review"

def parse_findings(name, text):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    out, section = [], ""
    i = 0
    in_fixed_table = False
    while i < len(lines):
        l = lines[i]
        if LATER_ROUND.match(l):
                    break
        ext = symbol_extent(lines, sym) if sym else None
        # a code snippet the finding quotes (`result=$(_fold_companion …)`) that
        # sits on exactly one head line — inside the cited symbol or near the
        # cited line when several lines carry it — is the strongest locus
        snip_anchors = []
        for _pos, s in snippets:
            s = re.split(r"\s*(?:…|\.\.\.)", s.strip(), maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
            if len(s) < 8 or "\n" in s:
                continue
            hits = [i for i, l in enumerate(lines, 1) if s in l]
            if not p.endswith(".md"):
                # in code, a hit on a comment-only line is documentation, not the site
                hits = [i for i in hits if not re.match(r"^\s*(#|//|/?\*|--)", lines[i - 1])]
            if len(hits) > 1 and ext:
                hits = [i for i in hits if ext[0] <= i <= ext[1]]
            if len(hits) > 1 and rng:
                hits = [i for i in hits if rng[0] - 40 <= i <= rng[1] + 40]
            if len(hits) == 1 and sum(1 for l in lines if s in l) == 1 and not has_secret(s) and "\t" not in s:
                if hits[0] not in [a for a, _ in snip_anchors]:
                    snip_anchors.append((hits[0], s))

head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:159 — The new `guard-yield.sh --check` CI step fails on every run. The PR never commits the "tracked" register `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, and `--check` treats a missing `$OUT` as drift and exits 1 (guard-yield.sh:422). Reproduced in a scratch checkout.
head/tests/unit/guard-origins.bats:120 — GO-9 (`guard-yield.sh --check` must be in sync) fails for the same reason: `grimoires/loa/guards.md` is absent from the change. Reproduced: "drift: grimoires/loa/guards.md differs from the generated register".
head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:37 — The `paths:` filters (push and pull_request) were not extended to the new inputs: `tools/cycle-ratio.sh`, `.claude/rules/**`, `.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml`, `.claude/data/floor.yaml`, `.claude/loa/**` (the generated hooks table) and `grimoires/loa/guards.md`. A PR that edits only the origin map or the floor skips the drift gate and the new suites.
head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39 — FS-2 can never fail. `$in` is used inside `def m(...)` but bound only afterwards (`. as $in | select(m($rules))`). jq rejects the filter at compile time ("$in is not defined", exit 3) on both sides of the `diff`, so two empty streams always compare equal. The floor-corpus snapshot is not checked at all.
head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:18 — On CI this suite always skips: the checkout is shallow and has no `origin/main` on pull_request, and on push to main the comparison is trivially equal. Together with the FS-2 defect, nothing in CI enforces the floor files or the floor corpus that the PR describes as "must not change".
head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:10 — The comment says "Both bats suites pin this file's sha256 (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant)", but only guard-origins.bats has the pin; floor-snapshot.bats has none.
head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:302 — The "too small to name" escape uses `abs(drop) <= base_spread`, but the pre-registered rule (docstring lines 20-23, suites `threshold`) says a recall loss needs the mean drop to *exceed* the baseline spread. With abs(), an arm whose mean recall *rises* by more than the spread, and that violates only the min-trial rule, is reported as `recall loss` (reproduced: baseline 0.5 flat, arm 0.2/1.0/1.0 gives "recall loss"). Use `drop <= base_spread`.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:266 — The `rule_files` toggle exits 0 with "removed: none present" when neither rule file exists in the sandbox, so the arm silently runs as its baseline. The header contract (lines 64-66) says "a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2"; the other toggles honour it.
head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:132 — `! grep -q 'Karpathy' …` (and line 133) is not the last command of AT-5. Bash/bats ignore `set -e` and the ERR trap for `!`-negated commands, so the assertion that the Karpathy section is gone can never fail. Use `run ! grep` or `! grep … || false`.
head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:152 — Same no-op negation in AT-7 (lines 152-153, and AT-8 at 166): the test's main claim, that the delta paragraph is removed from SKILL.md and the system prompt, is never checked.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:69 — `! grep -q 'must never be read' …` is a no-op (negated, not last), so the "previous-round section is never read" rule is untested. Breaking SKIP_SECTION still passes SC-1. The same no-op negation appears at lines 90, 91 and 143: the secret-leak check, the c.sh label check and the corpus.tsv row-removal check.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:141 — In `[ ! -e A ] && [ ! -e B ] && …` only the last test can fail the bats test (set -e ignores the earlier members of an && list). Removal of the fixture dir, the labels and the manifest is therefore unverified. The same applies at lines 79 and 154.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:159 — SC-6's "non-record fixture is refused" case never reaches the refusal. The fixture `pr-01` has no fixture.yaml, so the guard is skipped. The script then deletes pr-01, including its instruction templates, and crashes copying those templates. The test passes on exit 1 for the wrong reason.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:730 — `shutil.rmtree(fdir)` deletes any existing pr-NN directory that lacks fixture.yaml: the overwrite guard at line 295 only runs when fixture.yaml exists. Nothing refuses `--out pr-01`, which is the template source copied at lines 743-745. Seeding into it destroys the hand-made fixture and its templates, then fails.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:770 — When the no-secrets scan fails, the new fixture dir and label files are removed, but the previous good fixture was already deleted at line 730. The old manifest, both task yamls, the corpus.tsv row and a SHA256SUMS that lists deleted files are left behind, so `--check` fails, despite the message "nothing kept".
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:312 — Binary detection mis-parses rename paths. `git diff --numstat -M` prints renames in brace form (`d/{a => b}/x.bin`), and `split(" => ")[-1].strip("{}")` yields `b}/x.bin`. A renamed binary is therefore not excluded, and it is written through `redact()` (decode with replace, re-encode), which corrupts it.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:590 — The `sum(1 for l in lines if s in l) == 1` condition requires the snippet to be unique in the whole file. That undoes the in-symbol and ±40-line narrowing on lines 586-589, so the multi-hit case the comment at 574-576 describes can never produce an anchor.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:411 — Label provenance does not match the documented rule (header lines 36-39). `source_kind` labels every non-auditor, non-bridgebuilder file as `review` (not only engineer-feedback*/reviewer*). `parse_findings` ignores `name`, so bridgebuilder bullets and `### [SEV]` findings become labels, not just its "Fixed" table.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:251 — Reusing a batch is allowed whenever source and model match, but there is no resume. The whole plan reruns and appends to results.jsonl (duplicate trial numbers and stale error rows), STATUS counters restart, and MANIFEST.json is overwritten with possibly different arms or fixtures. The arms report then counts mixed and duplicated trials.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:327 — Each trial is verified against the *current* SHA256SUMS, which `seed-corpus-from-record.sh --approve/--build-manifest` rewrites. Relabelling a fixture mid-batch passes the check, so trials of one batch get graded against different labels. The header says "a drift stops the batch"; the check should compare against the digests taken at batch start.
head/evals/harness/compare-ab.py:72 — Every model with output in `models_used` now counts as model skew. execute-agent.sh pins only CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, and its own comments note that helper (haiku) calls appear in modelUsage. Any trial with a helper call now makes the A/B invalid (and every arm inconclusive in arms-report.py:145), a regression for previously valid comparisons.
head/evals/tests/run-arms.bats:58 — `[ ! -e "$T/argv" ]` cannot detect a CLI call. write_manifest (run-arms.sh:171) runs `$claude_bin --version` even in dry-run, and the stub returns before writing STUB_ARGV_FILE for `--version`. The "no CLI call" claim is untested, and it is in fact false.
head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:314 — The transport-failure heuristic greps agent-output.json (which carries the model's final text) as well as stderr, for broad words such as `network` and `5[0-9][0-9] `. Genuine agent failures can be retried and recorded as transport_error.
head/tests/unit/validate-artifact-sprint-kinds.bats:130 — The KINDS-9 skip guard (`2026-1[0-2]-`) does not match the rule start KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM=2026-10-14. A live plan dated 2026-10-01 to 10-13 is pre-rule and correctly warns, yet the test fails it. Plans from 2027 onward are skipped forever.
head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-kind-01.yml:6 — The comment claims the `.yml` extension keeps this task out of every run, but `run-eval.sh --skill reviewing-code` and the default all-tasks discovery both glob `*.yml`, so the kind fixture leaks into regular review-recall runs.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:754 — The FR-1.2b fence marker sits above the `if` instead of directly above its `emit_block` (line 758), unlike every other marker. It only passes guard-yield's 8-line window by luck; any growth of the condition breaks the register gate.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
This PR can't merge: my verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 26 findings, one per line, ending with that verdict line. I didn't touch anything under `pr/`.

**Merge blockers:**
- **CI will fail.** The new `guard-yield.sh --check` step in `bats-tests.yml` and test GO-9 both need `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, which the PR never adds. `--check` counts a missing file as drift. I rebuilt the repo in a scratch copy and GO-9 fails exactly this way.
- **The floor checks don't work.** FS-2 in `floor-snapshot.bats` has a jq scoping bug (`$in` is used before it's bound), so jq errors on both sides of the comparison. It ends up comparing two empty outputs and always passes; I confirmed the error. CI also checks out a shallow clone with no `origin/main`, so the whole floor-snapshot suite skips there.
- **The pre-registered verdict rule is wrong.** `arms-report.py:302` uses `abs(drop)`, so an arm whose recall *rises* can be reported as "recall loss".
- **One A/B arm can secretly run as the baseline.** The `rule_files` toggle in `execute-agent.sh` succeeds even when there's nothing to remove, although the script's own header says that case must exit 2.
- **Seeding can destroy data.** `seed-corpus-from-record.sh` deletes any `pr-NN` directory without a `fixture.yaml`, including `pr-01`, the template source it then tries to copy from. If the no-secrets scan fails, it leaves the corpus half-updated.

**Weak tests:** several assertions in `seed-corpus.bats`, `arm-toggles.bats` and `run-arms.bats` can never fail. Most are `! grep` lines that aren't the last command in their test, which bash never treats as a failure; others are `&&` chains where only the last check counts.

The rest are medium or low severity: batch reuse with no resume logic, the corpus hash checked mid-batch instead of at batch start, helper models now counted as model skew, a rename-path parsing bug, missing CI path filters, and a few doc/code mismatches.

**How I checked:** I reviewed the safety hook, `guard-yield.sh` and the origin map myself. The origin map, the fence and validator markers, and the floor set all match each other. Three subagents covered the eval harness, the seed corpus/grader, and the validator/tools/workflows. I re-checked their strongest claims myself (the jq error, the `abs()` logic, the toggle, the no-op assertions) before including them. `run-arms.sh` was reviewed by reading only, because the frozen PR doesn't include the corpus and scripts it needs to run.

- **Seeding can destroy data.** `seed-corpus-from-record.sh` deletes any `pr-NN` directory without a `fixture.yaml`, including `pr-01`, the template source it then tries to copy from. If the no-secrets scan fails, it leaves the corpus half-updated.

**Weak tests:** several assertions in `seed-corpus.bats`, `arm-toggles.bats` and `run-arms.bats` can never fail. Most are `! grep` lines that aren't the last command in their test, which bash never treats as a failure; others are `&&` chains where only the last check counts.

The rest are medium or low severity: batch reuse with no resume logic, the corpus hash checked mid-batch instead of at batch start, helper models now counted as model skew, a rename-path parsing bug, missing CI path filters, and a few doc/code mismatches.

**How I checked:** I reviewed the safety hook, `guard-yield.sh` and the origin map myself. The origin map, the fence and validator markers, and the floor set all match each other. Three subagents covered the eval harness, the seed corpus/grader, and the validator/tools/workflows. I re-checked their strongest claims myself (the jq error, the `abs()` logic, the toggle, the no-op assertions) before including them. `run-arms.sh` was reviewed by reading only, because the frozen PR doesn't include the corpus and scripts it needs to run.
